title: MTU fragmentation causing proxy 5xxs and retry amplification — containment + longterm fix
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers using Dedicated and Private deployments reported a pattern of transient 502/504 errors for streaming/generative requests. On investigation, failures correlated with customers that route traffic through an on-prem edge or a third‑party proxy that performs extra packet inspection and has a reduced MTU, causing TCP fragmentation and occasional proxy-side reassembly failures. The proxy responded with 5xx/504 which clients retried aggressively, amplifying load and causing degradation on Dedicated pools.

Impact: 3 paying customers experienced intermittent production errors and elevated latency spikes over a 4 hour window. Customer escalations opened to support and SRE. Traffic surge from automated client retries increased CPU and connection counts on several Dedicated nodes, contributing to increased error rates for collateral tenants.

Root cause: Path MTU mismatch + deep packet inspection proxies that drop fragmented packets in certain streams (large initial headers + streaming chunking pattern). Our edge expected normal reassembly; however these proxies returned opaque 5xx or reset connections, which our client SDKs retried quickly (default exponential backoff poorly tuned), generating retry amplification and admission pressure.

Immediate mitigation implemented (hotfixes):
- Deployed edge rule that recognizes the fingerprint (large streaming request headers + low MSS path) and falls back to a non-fragmenting ingress path (nginx sidecar tweak to set TCP MSS to 1200) for affected tenant CID ranges.
- Added a temporary per-tenant retry cap (server-side) to limit retries accepted from same client identity to 3 per 60s window, preventing amplification.
- Published support KB to customers with steps to detect MTU issues (ping -M do + packet sizing) and recommended SDK config to enable jittered exponential backoff.

Long-term plan / proposed fixes:
1) Edge: upstream kernel-level MSS clamp configurable per-route and automated detection of fragmentation signatures. (runtime-1.20 target)
2) SDK: change default retry policy to include randomized jitter and a client-side max-retries-by-request-type; add explicit guidance for environments behind packet-inspecting proxies.
3) Admission controller: implement adaptive tenant admission that recognizes retry storms and automatically transitions tenants into a degraded-but-functional lane with strict concurrency & retry limits.
4) Observability: add an MTU/fragmentation signal to routing telemetry (edge logs + flow metadata), and synthetic probe coverage against common corporate proxies.
5) QA: add regression test harness that simulates MTU-restricted proxies and verifies streaming/generation flows under fragmentation.

Acceptance criteria: production errors reduced to baseline for affected customers, retry amplification prevented by admission controls, and at least one customer confirms restored SLA for their workload.
